title: Grokking Neural Networks
description: Watch a neural network suddenly 'get it' after appearing to only memorize. This demonstrates the grokking phenomenon - delayed generalization in neural networks.

whatIs.title: What is Grokking?
whatIs.description: Grokking is a fascinating phenomenon where neural networks suddenly 'get it' after appearing to only memorize. The network first achieves 100% training accuracy (memorization), then much later, test accuracy suddenly jumps (generalization). It's like when a student crams for an exam vs. truly understanding the material.

task.title: The Task: Modular Arithmetic
task.description: The network learns modular addition: (a + b) mod 67. For example, 45 + 30 mod 67 = 8. This seems simple, but discovering the underlying pattern (instead of memorizing all 2,278 possible combinations) requires the network to learn the mathematical structure of modular arithmetic.

why.title: Why Does Grokking Happen?
why.description: The key is HIGH weight decay (regularization). Without it, networks just memorize. With strong weight decay, the network is pushed toward simpler solutions that generalize. This takes time - the 'grokking' moment happens when the network finally discovers the generalizing solution.
